To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mobile phone-deliverable intervention, incorporating explicit reflection and implicit rewarding strategies to promote healthy snacking among adolescents, was not feasible and did not have an impact on healthy snacking.
the intervention was not able (due to low reach and app usage) to improve adolescents’ healthy snack intake.
a mobile phone-deliver intervention, incorporating explicit and implicit strategies, did not improve adolescents’ snack intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of an innovative intervention to improve adolescents’ eating habits and their determinants.
the development and evaluation of an intervention to improve the snacking habits of adolescents, with a focus on the role of implicit processes.
the development of a mobile phone application (app) for adolescents to improve snacking habits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intervention was not effective, but it is too early to draw definitive conclusions about the impact of the intervention.
the present intervention is not feasible and not effective.
a multicomponent intervention that combines both reflective and implicit strategies is needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and evaluated a mobile application that is able to increase awareness and knowledge on snacking habits in adolescents, but is unable to change their actual snacking habits.
a mobile phone-based intervention to change adolescents’ snacking behaviour did not have a significant impact on snacking behaviour.
the current study shows that the app did not have the expected effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of mobile phone applications for healthy eating interventions in adolescents needs further exploration and development.
it is important to consider the heterogeneity in reward sensitivity and the importance of the implicit reward pathway.
it may not be feasible to change adolescents’ snacking behaviour by means of an app.
